methodological_questions: Is a conditional lift in PULL_UP outcomes after PNR fail consistent across defensive units?
What share of units must show positive lift, and what median lift threshold applies, under the stated 70% and 2pp criteria?
How should units, PNR fail, and the lift baseline be defined so that the comparison is not confounded by shot quality, opponent, or play-type tagging?

historical_evidence.finding: PBP-derived shot-level PNR rates were calibrated and described by team (2024-25, 30 teams, half-court shots about 5994-6581). Rates were reported as descriptive, with no pass/fail gate, and later logs cite calibrated PNR at about 17.9-19.6% of possessions. Validation was not recorded.

Defensive PPP allowed and possession share by play type, RS vs playoffs, 25 teams, minimum 30 possessions per cell. PNR share rose +12.1pp in playoffs, which the record says may reflect tagging differences. PULL_UP allowed PPP rose +0.341 and its share fell 7.6pp. No inferential test was run.

Named star suppressors by lineup and forced play type, with a minimum of 15 per play type and n of at least 30 for cited lineup cells. Example: Giannis forced PULL_UP PPP 0.848 (-0.540 vs preferred DRIVE). The record notes no placebo or matching, and later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Superstar suppression profiles including sequential triggering. Rank-1 suppressor deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control. The record flags an OTHER artifact.

TOV_FORCE lifts in a 4-game sample shrank about 50% or more under re-route and PT-shift controls (for example ORL +8.4 to +3.7pp). The record states net lift is model-implied rather than observed, and the counter-channel check was often an additive surrogate at n<10.

Within-game adaptation toward counters showed an adapter advantage of about +0.058 PPP. The record links this to selection and regression to the mean, so the apparent counter benefit was not established as causal.

Adapter falsification tests: wrong-way and no-signal groups did not behave as the adaptation hypothesis predicted, the scheme-vote gradient did not hold, and next-game carryover was not significant (Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842).

On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) were confidently labeled for only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of on-ball possessions, and switches_on was unpopulated. The record treats label coverage as insufficient.

Calibrated simulation versus Elo and lineup baselines: validation win accuracy 68.9% fell to 54.8% on holdout (155 games), below Elo at 58.1% and lineup +/- at 64.5%. The record flags the collapse as an artifact, and the authors' own holdout did not support the claimed benefit.

Simulation kernel vs linear team+opponent+play_type baseline: deterministic kernel R=+0.466 vs linear +0.467 (gap 0.001). The record classes this as a powered null, meaning the added complexity did not beat the simple model.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive schemes from matchup and PBP fields to support scheme-conditional analysis
failed_approaches.why: Labels were confident for only 3.3% to 14.9% of possessions, switches_on was not populated, and the record cites label error and small sample as limiting.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Adapter counter-response falsification (asymmetry, confidence gradient, next-game carryover)
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: label error and selection or regression to the mean; the carryover test was not significant.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game adaptation toward SHOULD counters as evidence of PPP gain
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: selection and regression to the mean (LIM:selection_or_regression_to_the_mean).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Calibrated simulation beating simple baselines out of sample
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: validation-to-holdout collapse, and the simple baseline was not beaten on holdout.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star suppressor identification by lineup and forced play type
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching was run, so the gaps could not be separated from artifacts; later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking rank-1 suppressors across many player-play-type cells
failed_approaches.why: Deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE and no multiple-comparison control was applied.

evidence_establishes: The project has built PBP-derived PNR and PULL_UP possession labels for 30 teams and several seasons, and these labels have been calibrated (FAM:SF-APPM-058, FAM:SF-APPS-012).
Defensive play-type splits by team and by regular season versus playoffs are computable at roughly 30 units with minimum-cell rules of 30 possessions (FAM:SF-APPS-012).

Earlier counter and suppression claims in this project, including those tested with falsification, have repeatedly failed to hold as causal or out of sample (FAM:SF13, FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF-PAP-098, FAM:SF-CHT-009).
PNR share estimates may depend on tagging conventions that shift across contexts, such as the playoff +12.1pp jump (FAM:SF-APPS-012).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests PULL_UP lift conditional on PNR fail, or the 70%-of-units and median >2pp criteria.
No retrieved record defines PNR fail, the unit of analysis, or the baseline against which lift is measured for this question.
No retrieved record shows that PULL_UP outcomes after PNR fail differ from matched non-PNR PULL_UP outcomes.
No retrieved record reports a placebo, negative control, or holdout-season test for this specific counter relationship.
No retrieved record reports validated PNR fail labels or their error rate.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a conditional descriptive contrast with an undefined PNR-fail event, so its answer depends mainly on how PNR fail and the lift baseline are defined.
With about 30 defensive units, the consistency rule (at least 70% positive) is a coarse test, and the 2pp median threshold will be sensitive to shot-quality and opponent mix.
Because PNR fail is defined by the defense's outcome (a defensive PNR that fails), selecting possessions by fail status can produce outcome-derived bias in PULL_UP outcomes.
The historical pattern suggests that a positive raw lift is likely to shrink or vanish under matching, which argues for treating a positive result as provisional until falsification passes.
Playoff data for 2025-26 is partial until 2026-06-21, so it must be excluded for a 2026-05-23 analysis to avoid leakage or mixing complete and incomplete data.
uncertainties: The definition of PNR fail (for example, possession ends with no shot, shot by a non-PNR action, or a turnover or foul) is not stated and is the largest source of ambiguity.
The units are not defined; the question could refer to defensive teams, team-seasons, or team-opponent pairs.
The unit of lift (percentage-point make rate, eFG, or PPP) is not stated; '2pp' may refer to a different scale.
The tagging error rate of PNR and PULL_UP labels from the PBP is not reported in any retrieved record.
No retrieved record gives the per-unit sample of PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possessions, so statistical power is unknown.
Whether a 2025-26 regular-season snapshot differs from earlier seasons (drift) has not been assessed.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical records did not answer the question, but they showed that earlier counter and suppression claims in this project were often artifacts, untestable, or inconclusive, and that PNR tagging and label coverage are fragile. This moved the decision from an unconditional proceed to proceed_with_changes: definitions must be fixed in advance, placebo and matched-baseline tests are required, and the primary claim must be held to a holdout season before any counter is called league-wide.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR fail is defined by the defensive outcome, and the labels come from PBP-derived possession records, so the fail split may partly encode the result being measured.
PNR and PULL_UP tagging differences (for example the playoff PNR share jump of +12.1pp in FAM:SF-APPS-012) could make unit-level counts unreliable.
With about 30 units and per-unit PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP counts that are likely small, a 2pp median threshold may not be reliably distinguished from zero.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record answers the PULL_UP-after-PNR-fail conditional lift question. Related records provide calibrated PNR shares and defensive play-type splits (descriptive), and several counter and suppression claims were later classified as artifacts, untestable, or inconclusive. These support caution and falsification, but they do not settle this question.

risks.text: Selecting possessions by defensive PNR fail status and then measuring PULL_UP outcomes can mix the selection and the outcome.
PBP-derived PNR and PULL_UP tags may be mis-assigned, and tagging conventions appear to differ between regular season and playoffs.
Per-unit lift estimates from small possession counts may be unstable and should be reported with uncertainty intervals or shrinkage.
Unit-level PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP counts may be too small for the 2pp median threshold; power must be computed before analysis.
Some defensive units may have too few PNR-fail possessions to form a valid cell, as with the minimum-30-possession rule used in FAM:SF-APPS-012.
Shot distance and quality, opponent offensive quality, pace, lineup, and game state may drive PULL_UP outcomes independently of PNR fail.
Units selected for an extreme PNR-fail rate may show regression to the mean; this pattern was recorded as an artifact in FAM:SF13 and FAM:SF-APPA-001.
Without placebo play types or matched non-PNR baselines, a positive lift can be produced by the play-type mix, as in FAM:SF-CHT-009.
Testing PULL_UP and other counter play types across units and seasons inflates the chance of a spurious consistency pass; FAM:SF-APPM-022 shows this risk.
2025-26 playoff data was partial before 2026-06-21, and any use of future possessions or incomplete games would leak information.
Play-type tendencies and defensive schemes change across seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooled lift may reflect drift.
The 70% consistency rule is interpreted against a base rate of unit-level positive lift that is unknown and may be high by chance under shared shot-quality trends.

design.estimand: Per-unit difference in PULL_UP outcome (points per possession, with make-rate in percentage points reported alongside) for possessions following a defensive PNR fail, relative to a matched baseline of PULL_UP possessions with no PNR fail, controlling for shot quality and opponent. The 2pp threshold must be restated on a fixed scale before analysis.
design.unit: Defensive team x season (primary); team-opponent-season as a sensitivity unit. Units with fewer than a pre-set minimum of PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP possessions are excluded or pooled with pre-declared rules.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 (complete), and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs, which are incomplete as of the 2026-05-23 analysis date. Playoffs are a separate pre-registered sensitivity analysis only after completion.
design.power: Before any analysis, run a simulation with the observed PNR-fail and PULL_UP counts per unit to estimate the probability of passing both criteria (at least 70% of units positive and median lift above 2pp) under plausible true effects of 0 and 2pp. Report the power and the minimum detectable effect; if power is below 0.8 under the plausible effect, report as uncertain rather than supported.
design.controls: Expected PPP from shot distance and shot zone; opponent offensive quality; pace; lineup or PT; game state (score margin, period); and PNR-fail rate of the unit. Use a hierarchical model with shrinkage for unit estimates, and report intervals rather than point lifts only.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo play types: the same test applied to SPOT_UP and DRIVE after PNR fail, which should show no counter effect by construction. (2) Placebo timing: lift computed from PULL_UP possessions with a shuffled PNR-fail label within unit-season. (3) Negative control: PULL_UP lift after a non-PNR initiator. (4) Holdout season: define the counter on 2022-23 to 2024-25 and test on 2025-26 regular season; the primary claim must replicate there.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary test (PULL_UP after PNR fail, consistency and median criteria). Apply Holm correction across any other counter play types or seasons examined. Report all tested play types, including null ones.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) at least 70% of units have positive lift with a confidence interval excluding zero on the holdout season, (b) median lift exceeds 2pp, (c) the placebo play types and shuffled-label tests show lift near zero, and (d) power was at least 0.8 for the plausible effect. If (a) or (b) pass but (c) or (d) fail, report artifact or uncertain. If power is too low, report uncertain. Do not describe the counter as league-wide unless all criteria hold.
design.data_version: NBA stats API PBP, substitution intervals, defensive matchup minutes, and box-score data for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Freeze the PNR and PULL_UP label definitions and the PBP extraction version before analysis, and record the extraction date. Exclude 2025-26 playoff data (partial before 2026-06-21).

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
